query: Consider the following context: Conventional material processing approaches often achieve strengthening of materials at the cost of reduced ductility. In that context, which method can be used for overcome the strength-ductility trade-off, and why?

generation.hypothesis: High-entropy alloys can overcome the strength-ductility trade-off in materials science.
generation.material_initial_state: Conventional materials with reduced ductility due to strengthening.
generation.intervention: Using high-entropy alloys with multiple principal elements.
generation.mechanism: Phase transformation strengthening and amorphization in extreme deformation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved strength and ductility in high-entropy alloys.
generation.uncertainty: Further research is needed to fully understand the mechanisms and properties of high-entropy alloys.
generation.falsification_experiment: Comparative study of high-entropy alloys and conventional materials under various conditions.
